leading_positions.synthesis: Six round-1 files name B014 as the preferred single prize part, all with the same set of laureates (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford), though citation wording differs. Andersson and Fredriksson say they moved from an opening trio containing Gali to this set after the discussion. Shared: nominal rigidities, the policy rule and the microfounded synthesis are distinct, load-bearing contributions; the work is mature (25-40 years); and critique after 2008 and 2021-22 has produced extensions rather than abandonment. Not shared or unresolved: every supporter records attribution as the main weakness (Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Gertler, Smets, Wouters are excluded by the three-person cap), and several accept that Gali in place of Calvo is a defensible swap (Hjalmarsson, Hassler). Non-supporters do not reject the science: Boppart, Enflo, Strömberg and Teorell list B014 as an alternative, Boppart calls it very important and fully mature, and Strömberg and Teorell say they would support it if a defensible narrower citation or attribution were agreed. Friberg does not list it as an alternative. The six explicit preferences equal the six-vote majority threshold under the modeling assumption, but these are stated round-1 preferences, not binding votes, and the chair is one of the six.

Strömberg and Teorell prefer a Kiyotaki-Moore pair for the collateral-constraint credit-cycle mechanism. Both dropped Gertler after the discussion. Shared with most colleagues: this has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and no round-1 file argues for adding Gertler. Eight other members (Andersson, Boppart, Dreber, Enflo, Fredriksson, Friberg, Hassler, Krusell) list B003 as an alternative. Supporters argue it is a distinct mechanism from the 2022 banks-and-crises recognition. Not shared: Hassler, Krusell, Dreber and Hjalmarsson see the 2022 prize as narrowing its marginal room, and the original paper is theoretical with limited direct empirical identification. Strömberg and Teorell both concede B014 has the larger footprint in practice.

Boppart and Enflo prefer a Melitz-Helpman pair for firm heterogeneity and selection in trade. Both exclude Redding as a later, quantitative extension of the core idea. Shared: Melitz (2003) is the clear originator, the framework has been tested for 20+ years in firm-level data, and the two-name attribution is stable across everyone who ranked it. Not shared: Krusell, Dreber, Strömberg, Fredriksson and Hjalmarsson cite the Krugman 2008 overlap and the priority claims of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum (not credited on the entry), and Enflo notes thinner top-three support. Both supporters list B003 as an alternative, and Enflo also lists B014. Hjalmarsson, Strömberg and Friberg list B047 as an alternative.

Friberg alone prefers B032 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) for founding modern political economics, with a citation tied to the framework and research agenda rather than settled causal magnitudes. Dreber, Krusell and Teorell list it as an alternative. Open issues he records: the 2024 institutions prize as a neighbouring recent award, identification in cross-country constitutional estimates, whether Besley belongs alongside the other two, and his own possible familiarity bias given that political economy is outside his field.

areas_of_agreement: All eleven round-1 files propose a single prize part with two or three laureates, and all express attribution concerns as well as scientific ones.

No round-1 file prefers B006, B030, B018 or any other shortlisted entry. Hassler moved from B030 (first at opening) to B014 and now lists B030 only as a low-ranked alternative, citing no colleague support and an unresolved distinctiveness question relative to the 2008 trade prize.

Several files (Boppart, Enflo, Friberg, Hassler, Krusell) agree Helpman cannot be credited in both B047 and B030 and that the committee must choose where his strongest contribution lies. Those five regard B047 as the stronger trade case.
On B003, the pair Kiyotaki-Moore is the common attribution; Strömberg and Andersson moved off an opening trio that included Gertler, and no file argues for restoring him.
Several members (Dreber, Teorell, Boppart, Friberg) state explicitly that first-place or top-three counts are not evidence of scientific merit and that they argue from the common criteria.

B014, B003 and B047 are each described by members across specialities as mature, with decades of testing. The disagreement is about attribution, overlap with prior prizes and recent performance, not about whether the underlying work is original.
scientific_disputes: Whether the 2008 crisis, the zero lower bound, the 2021-23 inflation and the heterogeneous-agent critique weaken B014. Supporters read them as extensions of the framework (Hassler, Krusell, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson, Dreber). Andersson, Boppart and Dreber list the performance question as unsettled, and Krusell notes that representative-agent versions are widely seen as superseded.

Whether earlier monetary and macro prizes (Lucas, Sargent and Sims, Kydland and Prescott, Bernanke 2022) leave room for B014. Supporters argue that none recognised the pricing friction and policy rule. Boppart, Dreber, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson and Hassler flag possible saturation.

Whether B003 is distinct from the 2022 prize. Strömberg, Teorell and Fredriksson see collateral-driven amplification as a different mechanism from bank-run and Great Depression credit-channel work. Hassler, Krusell and Dreber see narrower marginal distinctiveness. Hjalmarsson, Strömberg and Teorell also note limited direct empirical identification in the original paper.

Whether selection and the extensive margin in B047 are a distinct step beyond the new trade theory recognised in 2008 (Enflo, Boppart, Friberg say yes). Krusell, Dreber, Fredriksson and Hjalmarsson raise the overlap. Boppart also notes that how much of the welfare-gain result comes from selection versus structural assumptions is debated.
Whether the Protection for Sale model in B030 has robust empirical support. Hassler himself notes mixed support, and Boppart, Enflo, Friberg and Krusell cite that point.

Whether B032's cross-country constitutional estimates meet modern identification standards (Friberg, Teorell) and whether the 2024 institutions prize addresses a different question and method (Friberg) or an adjacent one.

Whether game-theory prizes in 2005, 2007, 2012 and 2020 reduce the marginal case for B006 (Hassler, Andersson, Dreber), and whether Wolinsky's and Binmore's shares are justified. Andersson keeps B006 only as an alternative.
On B018, Dreber would limit credit to Piketty and Saez because wealth and offshore estimates are contested. Fredriksson lists the data-construction versus wealth-measurement trade-off as unresolved.
attribution_disputes: B014 third name: Calvo (pricing friction as the primitive of the New Keynesian Phillips curve) versus Gali (development, estimation and empirical grounding). Six supporters hold Calvo, Taylor and Woodford, but Hjalmarsson would not object strongly to a Gali swap and Hassler accepts his case if the citation is weighted to the empirical framework. Boppart's opening trio (shortlist) was Woodford, Gali, Taylor, and his round-1 file does not restate a trio.

B014 estimated-DSGE strand: Christiano, Eichenbaum and Evans (shock identification, medium-scale model), Smets and Wouters, and Gertler are excluded by a three-person cap. Andersson says the CEE claim is not derivative, and Fredriksson wants wording that does not claim the estimated tradition. Whether a citation naming pricing friction, rule and synthesis implicitly ranks the omitted contributors lower is unresolved.

B014 citation scope: Boppart observes that Calvo's and Taylor's older contract-pricing and rule insights differ from the Woodford and Gali synthesis, so the committee must say what it is crediting. Fredriksson asks whether Calvo's compact modelling device is a discovery in the sense the committee usually rewards. Strömberg says the citation must specify pricing friction, rule or integrated framework.

B047: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Hopenhayn are not credited but have parallel or antecedent claims. Redding is a credited name on the entry that Boppart and Enflo exclude. Helpman's placement between B047 and B030 is open.

B003: Gertler's claim runs through B014 and through the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist lineage, where Bernanke is a 2022 laureate. Most files conclude that adding him blurs attribution across two entries.
B032: whether Besley belongs alongside Persson and Tabellini or whether a narrower pair is preferable (Friberg).
B006: whether Binmore's contribution should count against the Rubinstein-Wolinsky pair (Andersson).
maturity_disputes: B014 is 25-40 years old and in policy use, but several members (Hassler, Krusell, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson) record the concern that a prize could reward a stage of development that heterogeneous-agent work may supersede. Supporters treat the same evidence as showing a framework that is extended rather than discarded.

B003 is about three decades old and tested by the 2008 crisis and a large quantitative literature, but its original contribution is theoretical and direct empirical identification came largely from later work.
B047 has 20+ years of firm-level testing. Enflo treats the absence of a trade prize since 2008 as favourable timing, whereas Boppart explicitly says timing is not merit.
B032 rests on 25+ years of work, but the neighbouring 2024 prize and the identification issues are cited as recency or robustness risks.
B006 is four decades old, and Andersson sees no timing risk, whereas Hassler and Dreber weigh recent game-theory recognition.
Wealth and offshore estimates in B018 are newer and still contested (Dreber, Fredriksson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair (Hassler): preferred B014 and is one of the six explicit supporters. He discloses co-authorship with Krusell, Boppart and Friberg and IIES colleagueship with Krusell and Boppart. He reports no apparent connection to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, or the B003 and B030 candidates. His 2018 speech and the 2018 background citing his own work are not connected to a shortlisted candidate. This summary was written from the round-1 files alone.

Krusell: B014 supporter. Co-author of Hassler and Boppart. His field of heterogeneous-agent macro extends or criticises the B014 framework. He notes a possible IIES institutional connection to Persson (B032, alternative only) while noting that his profile does not state Persson's affiliation.

Boppart: B047 supporter. Frequent co-author of Krusell and Hassler, IIES colleague of both. Long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow (B013, not in his preferred configuration). His field is adjacent to B047. His inference that he may have helped draft the 2025 Scientific Background is not documented.

Friberg: B032 supporter. Co-authored with Hassler and Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026). His file states a public marriage to Magdalena Andersson and an SSE affiliation in Stockholm. He reports no link to shortlisted candidates and notes B032 is outside his field.

Teorell: B003 supporter. Co-authored a Governance paper with Torsten Persson (B032, alternative only) and notes Persson is at Stockholm University in a different department. B032 is close to his own field. He also gave the 2024 presentation speech.

Strömberg: B003 supporter. Thematic proximity to John Moore's incomplete-contracts and debt lineage and presentation of the 2016 contract-theory prize. He flags possible familiarity bias toward contracting-based mechanisms.

Fredriksson: B014 supporter. Institutional overlap with the IIES macro group (Hassler, Krusell) at Stockholm University, 2010-17, but no co-authorship. Andersson: B014 supporter. Field adjacency to B006 (alternative) and a possible familiarity bias toward theory. Dreber, Enflo and Hjalmarsson report no apparent connection to shortlisted candidates.
Disclosed only; none adjudicated. All files rely on background knowledge for priority and attribution and none claims independent verification.
questions_for_round2: B014 third name: if the citation is framed around the pricing friction, the policy rule and the microfounded synthesis, should the third laureate be Calvo or Gali? Would any member change the name if the citation were weighted instead toward the empirical and estimated framework (Hjalmarsson and Hassler have said they would be open to this)?

B014 scope: can a three-person citation be worded so that it does not imply a ranking against Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler? Please give specific wording, or say if the cap makes the attribution problem unresolvable.

Strömberg and Teorell said they would support B014 if a defensible narrower citation or attribution were agreed. What wording or attribution would meet that condition, and do the six B014 supporters accept it?

B014 versus B003: B003's Kiyotaki-Moore attribution is undisputed in the files. Beyond attribution, which criterion (breadth of practical influence, durability, marginal distinctiveness after 2022) should place B014 ahead of B003 or the reverse, and what evidence would change your ordering?

Post-2021 inflation and heterogeneous-agent critique: is the evidence best read as an extension of the framework or as grounds for caution on maturity? Does any member who reads it the other way want to state the specific observation that would settle the question, as Hassler and Dreber have invited?

Prior-recognition overlap: how much weight should the 2022 prize (B003), the 2024 prize (B032), the 2008 trade prize (B047, B030) and the 2005-2020 game-theory prizes (B006) carry relative to merit, and can the committee apply a consistent standard across these entries?

B047: can a Melitz-Helpman citation be worded around selection and reallocation so that it does not overstate priority relative to Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and Hopenhayn, and is excluding Redding acceptable to members who list B047 as an alternative (Hjalmarsson, Strömberg, Friberg)?

B047, B032 and B003 supporters: is there any condition under which you would move your first preference to B014? Alternatively, does any member who prefers B014 now regard B003 or B047 as the better prize if their stated attribution or overlap reservation about B014 is not resolved?
summary.chair_observation: Round-1 files record six explicit preferences for B014 with an identical trio (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford), two each for B003 and B047, and one for B032. These are stated preferences from the files, not binding votes, and six equals the majority threshold only under the modeling assumption. The chair is one of the six, and several of the B014 supporters share co-authorship or institutional ties with the chair, which the summary discloses without adjudicating. Every B014 supporter also records attribution as the main weakness, and two members preferring B003 say they would support B014 if a defensible citation were found. The merit of the underlying work is mostly not contested, so round 2 turns on citation drafting, how prior-prize overlap is weighed, and how the post-2021 evidence bears on maturity.
